slots.label: posterior-probability misconception
slots.description: There is a 95% probability that the true mean lies inside this specific interval.
slots.repair: That sounds natural, but in the usual frequentist interpretation it is not quite right. The 95% describes the long-run reliability of the method, not the probability that this fixed interval contains the fixed mean.
slots.repairQuestion: If we repeated the same sampling and interval-construction process many times, what proportion of the newly computed intervals would contain the true population mean?
slots.repairCriteria: Mark this misconception repaired when the learner says, in any wording, that repeated or newly computed intervals would sometimes contain the true population mean and about 95% would contain it in the long run. If the tutor's repair question just referred to newly computed intervals, pronouns such as they, them, it, each one, or repetitions may refer to those intervals and should be interpreted in that context. Do not require the learner to restate the fixed-parameter distinction to repair this misconception; that is a separate expectation.

slots.label: individual-values misconception
slots.description: The interval means 95% of individual observations fall between 42 and 50.
slots.repair: This interval is about uncertainty in the population mean, not the spread of individual observations.
slots.repairQuestion: Is this confidence interval estimating individual observations, or is it estimating the population mean?
slots.repairCriteria: Mark this misconception repaired when the learner identifies the population mean as the target of the interval, or clearly rejects individual observations/scores/data points as the target. Do not require a full long-run coverage explanation to repair this misconception.

slots.label: sample-statistics-inside-interval misconception
slots.description: The interval means 95% of sample means, future sample means, or future confidence intervals will fall between 42 and 50.
slots.repair: The 95% is not about future sample means or future intervals landing inside [42, 50]. It is about how often intervals built the same way contain the true population mean.
slots.repairQuestion: In the repeated-sampling picture, is each new interval trying to fall inside [42, 50], or trying to contain the true population mean?
slots.repairCriteria: Mark this misconception repaired when the learner says each new interval is trying to contain the true population mean, or clearly rejects the idea that new intervals or future sample means must fall inside [42, 50].

slots.text: If we repeated the same sampling and interval-construction process many times, what proportion of the newly computed intervals would contain the true population mean?
Is this confidence interval estimating individual observations, or is it estimating the population mean?
In the repeated-sampling picture, is each new interval trying to fall inside [42, 50], or trying to contain the true population mean?

A 95% confidence interval means that if we repeatedly sampled from the same population and built intervals the same way, about 95% of those intervals would contain the true population mean. For this particular interval, the true mean is fixed, so it is either inside the interval or it is not.
